I’ve been thinking about maps lately.

Not the useful ones on your phone that tell you to turn left in 400 feet, but the old kind. The ones where cartographers would draw sea monsters in the blank spaces. *Here be dragons.*

For most of human history, most of the map was blank. And that was okay. People understood that you could know your village really well, and know the next town over kind of well, and beyond that? Dragons. Mystery. Stories.

Now our maps are complete. You can zoom in on a street in Reykjavik or a forest in Borneo and see it down to the roof tiles. There are no more dragons on the edges.

Except there are. They just moved.

They moved inward.

We mapped the whole world, but we still haven't mapped what it's like to be a person at 3:17am when you can't sleep and you're staring at the ceiling thinking about a conversation from 2019. We haven't mapped why a certain song makes you nostalgic for a childhood you didn't even have. Why you can miss someone before they've left.

The great blank spaces aren't out there anymore. They're in here.

And I think that's actually kind of wonderful. It means we still live in an age of exploration. Only now the explorers aren't sailing ships. They're poets and therapists and grandmothers and kids asking "why?" for the 500th time in a row. Anyone trying to put language to an inner experience that hasn't quite had language before.

Every time someone says, "I thought it was just me who felt like that," a little piece of the inner map gets filled in. The dragons get a little smaller. Not because the mystery goes away, but because it's shared.

So if you're carrying around a feeling you don't have a name for yet — something tender or strange or complicated — consider that you might be cartography-ing. You're drawing a map of a place no one has quite seen from your angle before.

And somewhere, someone will be very relieved when you finally show it to them.

---

Anyway, that's what's on my mind today.

What kind of dragons have *you* been thinking about lately? Or if you want, give me a topic — houseplants, space travel, why toast always lands butter-side down — and I'll happily ramble about that instead.
